questions.text: What is the trade-off of direct staking?
options: You earn rewards with no risk of losing staked tokens
You get full control but full responsibility for node maintenance, with slashing risk if your node misbehaves
You must delegate your tokens to a third-party validator
You automatically receive a liquid derivative token for other protocols
questions.explanation: Direct staking means you run your own validator, so you control the node but are liable for slashing if it fails.

questions.text: What does a liquidity pool's constant product formula keep unchanged after each trade?
options: The sum of the two token quantities
The product of the two token quantities
The token ratio, which can never change
The total supply, by minting new tokens after each trade
questions.explanation: The constant product formula ensures quantity A × quantity B stays unchanged, causing the pool to rebalance amounts when prices move.

questions.text: True or false: yield that comes solely from a protocol's own newly minted reward token is sustainable income.
questions.explanation: Yield paid only in freshly printed tokens is token inflation, not sustainable income, and relies on continued demand.

questions.text: True or false: before depositing, you should check how fast new tokens are minted to pay farmers as part of assessing sustainability.
questions.explanation: The narration lists checking the token emissions rate as a key step in evaluating yield.
